questions.statement: Which word refers to the mother of your mother or the father of your father?
questions.context: In a fifth-grade class in Bogota, students present a drawing of their family tree.

options.feedback: The parents of your parents are your grandparents.
A cousin is the child of your aunt or uncle.
A sister is a female sibling of the same parents.
A niece is the daughter of your brother or sister.

questions.explanation: Recognizing extended family vocabulary in English (grandparents, cousins, siblings, nieces).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Who is Diego in relation to the speaker?
questions.context: Read: "This is my family. My mother is Maria and my father is Carlos. I have one brother named Diego."

options.feedback: The text says "I have one brother named Diego", so Diego is the brother.
An uncle is the brother of your mother or father, not the speaker's sibling.
A cousin is the child of an aunt or uncle, not a sibling.
A grandfather is the father of your mother or father.

questions.explanation: Inferring family relationships from short descriptive sentences in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct possessive adjective to complete: "I love _____ parents very much."
questions.context: A student writes: "My family is small. There are four people in my family."

options.feedback: "My" is the possessive adjective for the first person singular (I).
"Your" is used with the second person (you).
"His" is used with third person singular masculine (he).
"Their" is used with third person plural (they).

questions.explanation: Using possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, our, their) in basic English sentences.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly describes Sofia's family using the verb "to be"?
questions.context: A girl named Sofia introduces her family in front of the class in Medellin.

options.text: Sofia is the daughter of Juan and Paula.
options.feedback: "Is" agrees with the third person singular subject "Sofia".

options.text: Sofia are the daughter of Juan and Paula.
options.feedback: "Are" is used with plural subjects, not with "Sofia".

options.text: Sofia am the daughter of Juan and Paula.
options.feedback: "Am" is only used with the first person singular subject "I".

options.text: Sofia be the daughter of Juan and Paula.
options.feedback: "Be" is the base form and is not used as a main verb in present simple.

questions.explanation: Conjugating "to be" (am, is, are) according to the subject in simple English sentences.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete with the correct Present Simple form: "My mother _____ dinner every evening."
questions.context: A student in Cartagena describes roles: "My mother cooks every day and my father works in an office."

options.feedback: With third person singular (my mother), the verb adds -s: cooks.
"Cook" without -s is used with plural subjects (we, they) or I/you.
"Cooking" requires the auxiliary verb to be for the present continuous.
"Cooked" is the past simple form, not used for daily routines in present.

questions.explanation: Applying the third-person singular -s rule in the Simple Present tense in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What can you infer about Laura's family from the text?
questions.context: Read: "Laura has two sisters. Their names are Ana and Paula. Ana is tall and Paula is short. They all live in Cali."

options.text: Laura has two sisters named Ana and Paula, and they live in Cali.
options.feedback: The text states Laura has two sisters and that they all live in Cali.

options.text: Laura has no siblings and lives in Bogota.
options.feedback: The text says she has two sisters, so this contradicts the passage.

options.text: Ana and Paula are Laura's cousins from another city.
options.feedback: The text clearly identifies Ana and Paula as Laura's sisters.

options.text: Laura is an only child who lives alone in Cali.
options.feedback: The text says she has two sisters, so she is not an only child.

questions.explanation: Synthesizing explicit details (names, number, city) to draw a correct inference about a family description.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly uses the possessive form to relate Mateo and Pedro?
questions.context: Compare: "Pedro is 40 years old and he is a father. His son Mateo is 10 years old."

options.feedback: The possessive "'s" with Pedro indicates the relationship of father to son.
"Mateo" is singular and requires the verb "is", not "are".
The structure "Pedro's is" is ungrammatical in English.
The structure reverses the relationship and is not grammatical.

questions.explanation: Analyzing the use of the Saxon genitive ('s) to express family relationships in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the main idea of this paragraph about family?
questions.context: Read the paragraph: 'Family is important because members support each other. In many Colombian families, grandparents, parents, and children share daily activities like cooking, studying, and celebrating together.'

options.text: Family members support each other and share important daily activities.
options.feedback: The paragraph emphasizes mutual support and shared activities within the family.

options.text: Only grandparents are important in a Colombian family.
options.feedback: The paragraph mentions grandparents, parents, and children, not only grandparents.

options.text: Family members should never spend time together.
options.feedback: The paragraph promotes shared activities, the opposite of never spending time together.

options.text: Studying and cooking are unimportant in family life.
options.feedback: The paragraph lists studying and cooking as examples of shared family activities.

questions.explanation: Evaluating the main idea of a short expository paragraph about family roles and values.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which animal is known as the largest land mammal with a long trunk and big ears?
questions.context: In a science class about animals at a school in Medellin, students learn about large wild animals.

options.feedback: Elephants are large land mammals with trunks and big ears.
Lions are big cats with manes, not animals with trunks.
Monkeys are primates that climb trees.
Rabbits are small domestic or wild rodents with long ears.

questions.explanation: Basic vocabulary recognition of animal names and physical characteristics in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Where do wild tigers usually live in their natural habitat?
questions.context: Read this short sentence: "Tigers have sharp teeth and dark stripes on their fur."

options.feedback: Wild tigers live in jungles, forests, and grasslands.
Oceans are marine habitats for fish and whales.
Barns are for domestic animals like cows and horses.
Wild tigers do not live in residential gardens.

questions.explanation: Understanding animal habitats and associating wild species with their natural environments.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence correctly: "Eagles _____ powerful wings and can fly very high."
questions.context: A teacher shows a picture of an eagle flying high over the Andes mountains in Colombia.

options.feedback: "Eagles" is plural, so it takes the verb form "have".
"Has" is used with singular subjects (he, she, it / eagle).
"Is" is a singular form of the verb to be.
"Having" is a present participle and needs an auxiliary verb.

questions.explanation: Subject-verb agreement in the Simple Present tense with plural nouns (Eagles have).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why do giraffes have long necks according to the context?
questions.context: Read the text: "Giraffes are the tallest animals in the savannah. They eat leaves from high tree branches."

options.text: To reach and eat leaves from tall trees.
options.feedback: Their long necks allow them to reach high branches easily.

options.text: To swim fast across deep rivers.
options.feedback: Giraffes do not use their necks for swimming.

options.text: To sleep underground during the night.
options.feedback: Giraffes are large surface animals and do not live underground.

options.text: To catch small fish in the sea.
options.feedback: Giraffes are herbivores that eat leaves, not fish.

questions.explanation: Extracting specific information from a short descriptive text in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct question to ask about an animal's diet: "What _____ pink river dolphins eat?"
questions.context: Two students discuss pink dolphins in the Amazon River in Colombia.

options.feedback: "Do" is the correct auxiliary verb for plural subjects like "pink river dolphins".
"Does" is used with third-person singular subjects (he, she, it).
"Is" is not the auxiliary verb for simple present action questions.
"Are" would require a present continuous verb (-ing form).

questions.explanation: Forming questions in the Simple Present tense using the auxiliary verb "do".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does the word "hibernation" mean in this passage?
questions.context: Read the short paragraph: "Bears sleep during the cold winter months. This long winter sleep is called hibernation. During this time, they do not eat or drink."

options.text: A long sleep during the winter season.
options.feedback: The passage explicitly defines hibernation as a long winter sleep.

options.text: Running fast across open green fields.
options.feedback: Bears rest during hibernation rather than running around.

options.text: Hunting for food in the river.
options.feedback: Bears do not hunt during hibernation because they do not eat.

options.text: Building nests on top of tall trees.
options.feedback: Bears sleep in caves or dens, not in tree nests.

questions.explanation: Inferring word meaning from context in simple English reading passages.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly compares the speed of these two animals?
questions.context: Compare two animals: "Cheetahs can run up to 100 kilometers per hour, while turtles move very slowly on land."

options.feedback: The comparative form "faster than" correctly compares cheetahs and turtles.
Incorrect because turtles move slowly while cheetahs run fast.
Incorrect meaning for the comparative "slower than".
Grammatically incorrect structure for comparative adjectives.

questions.explanation: Using comparative adjectives (-er than) to compare animal traits in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the main message and purpose of this poster?
questions.context: Read the poster statement: "Spectacled bears live in the cloud forests of Colombia. Their natural environment is disappearing because of deforestation. We must protect their home!"

options.text: To raise awareness about protecting spectacled bears and their forest habitat.
options.feedback: The text highlights habitat loss and calls for protecting their forest home.

options.text: To encourage people to keep wild spectacled bears as pets at home.
options.feedback: Wild bears cannot be domestic pets; the poster urges protecting their wild habitat.

options.text: To invite tourists to cut down trees in the cloud forest.
options.feedback: Deforestation is identified as a threat, not something to encourage.

options.text: To explain how to buy bear fur coats in city markets.
options.feedback: The poster advocates conservation, not commercial hunting.

questions.explanation: Evaluating the main purpose and message of an informational poster on wildlife conservation.
questions.subject: ingles
